glossary.benign: Not cancerous; does not invade or spread.
glossary.malignant: Cancerous; can invade nearby tissue and spread.
glossary.radiation exposure: Past exposure to ionising radiation, especially to the neck in childhood, which raises thyroid cancer risk.
glossary.incidental: Found by chance while looking for something else.
glossary.thyroid function tests: Blood tests of TSH and thyroid hormones (T4, T3).
glossary.hoarseness: A rough or weak voice, often from vocal cord nerve damage.
glossary.iatrogenic: Caused by medical treatment, such as surgery.
glossary.fixed mass: A lump stuck to surrounding tissue that cannot be moved, suggesting invasion.
glossary.tongue protrusion: Sticking the tongue out; a thyroglossal cyst rises when this is done.
glossary.metastasis: Spread of cancer from where it started to another part of the body.
glossary.von Hippel-Lindau: Inherited syndrome causing tumours such as haemangioblastomas, kidney cancer and phaeochromocytoma.
glossary.indeterminate: Cytology result that is neither clearly benign nor clearly malignant.
glossary.hypoechogenicity: Darker than surrounding tissue on ultrasound, a suspicious feature in a nodule.
glossary.irregular margins: Uneven, poorly defined edges on imaging, suggesting malignancy.
glossary.autonomous function: Making thyroid hormone without TSH control.
glossary.hyperthyroidism: Overactive thyroid with excess thyroid hormone.
glossary.surveillance: Regular monitoring over time for recurrence.
glossary.tumour marker: A blood substance that rises with a tumour and helps diagnose or monitor it.
glossary.neural crest: Embryonic cells that form nerves, adrenal medulla, melanocytes and thyroid C cells.
glossary.hyperplastic: Enlarged due to an increase in cell number.
glossary.colloid change: Swelling of thyroid follicles with stored colloid, a benign cause of nodules.
glossary.adenoma: A benign tumour of glandular tissue.
glossary.vascular invasion: Tumour cells growing into blood vessels.
glossary.lymphatics: Vessels that drain tissue fluid to lymph nodes.
glossary.inferior thyroid artery: Artery supplying the lower thyroid and parathyroids, closely related to the recurrent laryngeal nerve.
glossary.palsy: Paralysis or weakness from nerve damage.
glossary.devascularisation: Loss of blood supply to a tissue.
glossary.total thyroidectomy: Removal of the whole thyroid gland.
glossary.partial thyroidectomy: Removal of part of the thyroid, such as one lobe (hemithyroidectomy).
glossary.undetectable: Too low to be measured by the test.
glossary.parathyroid hormone: Hormone from the parathyroids that raises blood calcium.
glossary.tracer: A radioactive substance taken up by active thyroid tissue on a scan.
glossary.rapid growth: A lump enlarging quickly over weeks, a red flag for cancer.
glossary.thyroid cancer: Malignant tumour arising from thyroid cells.
